title: doc-deferral door: honour a reasoned not-a-deferral marker the way it already honours code fences
action: The bee close doc-deferral door (build_doc_deferral_door in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/drivers/close.rs) full-text scans every docs/ file a capped cell touched, and blocks on any line matching matches_deferral_prose (packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/decisions/verbs_read.rs — the stems defer/defers/deferred/deferring, later, for now, revisit when, revisit if) that carries no registered trigger citation. Only fenced code is exempt today. The result: a doc section that DOCUMENTS deferral machinery is unreadable to the door, because there the word is the subject matter, not a promise. Real incident, twice: closing features staging-optional and uat-stop-placement both blocked on the same prose in docs/handbook/register.md — the register entries for .bee/deferred-queue.jsonl and .bee/capture-queue.jsonl, plus a heading whose backtick span is the FILENAME '.bee/deferred-queue.jsonl' and gets tried as a trigger id. No honest remedy exists for those lines: registering a trigger for them would be a lie, and the prose cannot drop the word without losing the name of the file it documents. ADD a second exemption, modelled exactly on the existing in_fence toggle at close.rs:1075-1082. A line whose trimmed content matches the opening marker turns the exemption on; a line matching the closing marker turns it off; lines between are skipped. Opening marker: an HTML comment of the form <!-- bee:not-a-deferral: <reason> --> where <reason> is non-empty after trimming. Closing marker: <!-- /bee:not-a-deferral -->. An opening marker with an EMPTY or missing reason does NOT open the exemption — it is ignored, so the lines below it still block, and skipping stays a named act rather than an oversight (this is the same posture regen_obligation_ack takes on a cell). An unclosed exemption ends at end of file. The marker and a code fence nest independently — neither closes the other. Keep every other behavior byte-identical: the same scan file set, the same prose matcher, the same trigger-citation clearing, the same refusal shape and message. WIDEN the refusal's remedy line to name this marker as a third option beside registering a trigger and citing it, so a reader who hits a genuine false positive learns the escape from the message itself. Tests beside the existing door tests: a deferral line inside a reasoned marker does not block; the same line with the marker's reason empty DOES block; a line after the closing marker blocks again; an unclosed marker exempts to end of file; a code fence inside a marked block and a marked block inside a fence each behave independently; and the exact register.md shapes from the incident (the heading '### `.bee/deferred-queue.jsonl`', a prose line carrying 'deferred', and one carrying 'later') stop blocking once wrapped.
done_when: A reasoned <!-- bee:not-a-deferral: <reason> --> ... <!-- /bee:not-a-deferral --> block exempts the lines between it from the doc-deferral door; a reasonless marker exempts nothing; lines outside the block are unaffected; the fence exemption still works and the two nest independently; the refusal message names the marker as an option; and the close suite is green.
notes: Phase 1. dds-2 applies the marker to register.md and documents it — it depends on this cell shipping the syntax first.

truths: A deferral-shaped line inside a reasoned not-a-deferral block does not block the close.
The same marker with an empty or missing reason exempts nothing — the lines below it still block.
A deferral-shaped line after the closing marker blocks again.
An unclosed opening marker exempts to end of file.
The code-fence exemption still works, and a fence and a marker nest independently.
The scan file set, the prose matcher, and the trigger-citation clearing are all unchanged.
The refusal's remedy line names the marker as an option alongside registering and citing a trigger.
